description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Harrison Smith is returning to the Vikings on a one-year, $12.5 million deal.
items.impact: Smith is a Minnesota stalwart and franchise legend. He will provide Brian Flores' secondary with a veteran presence and ability.
items.title: Harrison Smith returning to Vikings on one-year deal

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Jon Weeks has been promoted to the Niners active roster. In a corresponding move, Brayden Willis has been released.
items.impact: Weeks will provide some special teams depth and the exit of Willis implies the return of George Kittle.
items.title: Jon Weeks promoted to Niners active roster

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Brayden Willis has been waived by the 49ers. In a corresponding move, they promoted long snapper Jon Weeks to the active roster.
items.impact: Willis' waiving likely signals the return of George Kittle, with Weeks providing some special teams depth. Willis is likely to be irrelevant for fantasy this season.
items.title: Brayden Willis waived by Niners

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was not practicing Saturday.
items.impact: Henderson has not practiced since August 24th, not a great sign for his availability come game time. The Patriots play the Seahawks on Wednesday, rather than a Thursday, giving Henderson one less day to get healthy. The Patriots first injury report comes out later today.
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) not practicing Saturday

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.desc: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
items.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.
items.title: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.desc: Running back J.K. Dobbins will "for sure" be the Denver Broncos' lead back this season, with three players set to have roles in the backfield, according to Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports.
items.impact: Dobbins was very successful in 2025 when he was healthy, averaging 5.0 yards per carry and rushing for 772 yards in 10 games. RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman will have roles, a regular trait for head coach Sean Payton's offenses. Due to injury risk and a congested backfield, Dobbins has a deflated ADP price as the half-PPR RB34, according to FantasyPros.
items.title: J.K. Dobbins will maintain Denver's RB1 role in 2026

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.desc: The Jacksonville Jaguars are "not going to stop talking" to wide receiver Parker Washington as both sides iron out a potential contract extension, says general manager James Gladstone.
items.impact: Gladstone said the team would not hesitate to carry contract discussions into the regular season as they aim to finalize a deal with their breakout wideout. Washington had 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns last season and carries an expert consensus ranking of WR29, according to FantasPros, into his fourth NFL season.
items.title: Parker Washington, Jaguars remain in contract talks

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.desc: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and the team "remain apart on several key elements" amid extension discussions ahead of the season opener.
items.impact: Gonzalez was noncommittal on his status for Week 1 amid contract disputes, which could put pressure on the Patriots to finish the deal. Some groundwork has been laid, and Gonzalez is expected to become the league's highest-paid cornerback, but finer details of the contract structure need to be finalized.
items.title: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots 'remain apart' on contract

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.desc: The Atlanta Falcons could name their starting quarterback, between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., as early as Monday, Sept. 7, ahead of Week 1.
items.impact: Nearly every team has named its starter for Week 1, but Atlanta has not formally announced its QB1. According to Ian Rapoport, Tagovailoa could have a "short leash" if named the starter as Atlanta waits for Penix to get healthy. Ideally, the Falcons hoped Tagovailoa would prove himself to be a steady, veteran presence, but Atlanta finds itself in limbo under center.
items.title: Tua Tagovailoa: Falcons could name starting QB soon

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Rams DL Aaron Donald is uncertain for the season opener next Thursday against the 49ers.
items.impact: Rams coach Sean McVay said he expects every player to travel with the team to Australia, which includes Donald. If he is cleared to play, it is likely he'll be on some sort of snap count.
items.title: Aaron Donald uncertain for Week 1

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Cowboys restructured the contract of DaRon Bland.
items.impact: Bland was one of three players to have his contract restructured by Dallas. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space.
items.title: DaRon Bland restructures contract with Cowboys

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Cowboys restructured the contract of Kenny Clark.
items.impact: Clark was one of three players to have his contract restructured by Dallas. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space
items.title: Kenny Clark restructures contract with Cowboys

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson's contract.
items.impact: Ferguson's $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space.
items.title: Jake Ferguson restructures contract with Cowboys

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Bears restructured the contract of T.J. Edwards.
items.impact: Edwards was one of three players who had their contracts restructured. The moves open $17 million in savings against the cap.
items.title: T.J. Edwards restructures contract with Bears

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Bears restructured the contract of Dayo Odeyingbo.
items.impact: Odeyingbo was one of three players who had their contracts restructured. The moves open $17 million in savings against the cap.
items.title: Dayo Odeyingbo restructures contract with Bears

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Bears restructured the contract of Joe Thuney.
items.impact: Thuney was one of three players who had their contracts restructured. The moves open $17 million in savings against the cap.
items.title: Joe Thuney restructures contract with Bears

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Texans agreed to terms with Tank Dell on a one-year, $1.7 million contract restructure.
items.impact: The move saves Houston $2 million against the cap. Dell is nearing his return from a gruesome knee injury he suffered late in the 2024 season.
items.title: Tank Dell restructures contract with Texans

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Bears RB D'Andre Swift left practice early on Thursday due to "a cramp."
items.impact: Swift was seen leaving practice "holding at his midsection or core area." It appears he should be good to go for the season opener next week.
items.title: D'Andre Swift left practice Thursday with a cramp

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Sam Okuayinonu (foot) is out against the LA Rams in the 49ers 2026 season opener.
items.impact: Okuayinonu didn't make the flight with the team down to Melbourne, but they left the door open for him to come down later. He will now try to get himself healthy and ready for Week 2.
items.title: Sam Okuayinonu (foot) out against LA Rams

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Devin Neal has been waived by the New Orleans Saints after reaching an injury settlement.
items.impact: Neal was originally placed on IR, but it seems the team has found a way to settle things and enact his release. He could find a new team, but cannot sign with the Saints again until at least three weeks from now.
items.title: Devin Neal waived by Saints

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Rome Odunze left Thursday's practice early with an apparent injury.
items.impact: Hammond notes that Odunze came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice. He tried to return to practice, but trainers wouldn't let him. This will remain something to monitor into next week.
items.title: Rome Odunze leaves practice early Thursday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Will Levis worked out for the Jets on Thursday.
items.impact: Levis was cut loose by the Titans this past weekend and subsequently cleared waivers. The second-round pick from 2023 spent all of last season on the IL after starting 21 games for the Titans over the previous two campaigns. Levis is looking to catch on with the Jets or another team, most likely as a third QB.
items.title: Will Levis works out for Jets

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Alec Pierce (ankle) practiced in full for the first time this year after a lengthy time off the field while recovering from ankle injuries.
items.impact: Pierce was limited in practice earlier this week, and this is the next big step for the newly anointed WR1 for the Colts on the road to full recovery and return to play. He will operate as the Colts primary deep threat this season when on the field, opening things up for Josh Downs and Tyler Warren over the middle and short areas.
items.title: Alec Pierce (ankle) practices in full on Thursday
